latest.title: Optimizing Amazon Quick Response Time
latest.description: Amazon Quick provides multiple layers for configuring metadata that helps the AI agent understand your data, apply business logic, and respond accurately. Each layer has a different impact on response speed. Placing the right information in the right layer is the single most impactful optimization you can make. This guide provides a decision framework with practical examples using an HR People Analytics case.

latest.title: Beyond the Plant Floor: Why Food Processing's Biggest AI Opportunity Is in the Back Office
latest.description: Food processors lose thousands of hours annually to manual back-office work in trade deductions, procurement, and financial reporting. This post breaks down which processes carry the highest manual burden and standardization potential, backed by real-world data showing 60-85% reductions in manual hours and millions in recovered revenue through agentic AI automation.

latest.title: Your Frontend App Isn't as Secure as You Think
latest.description: Your React app can render, deploy, and pass review while still shipping real security holes. Frontend security lives in layers, not a single setting. This post walks the four an attacker actually meets: XSS in your own code, server-side authorization, secrets that leak into the public bundle, and your npm dependencies. Plus AWS WAF as an easy outer layer.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.
